card.name: Ending of anatomical adjectives like subcapsular
card.fires_on: The final piece of an anatomical adjective split across tokens, mostly "ular" in "posterior subcapsular cataracts" and "ic" in "fundic gland polyps". It is strongest in steroid and PPI warning text.

modes.label: Subcapsular cataracts
modes.description: The ending "ular" of "subcapsular" right before "cataract" in steroid eye warnings.
modes.example: may increase the risk of posterior subcaps<<ular>> cataracts and glaucoma.

modes.label: Fundic gland polyps
modes.description: The ending "ic" of "fundic" before "gland polyps" in acid-reducer warnings.
modes.example: 5.13 Fundic Gland Polyps PPI use is associated with an increased risk of fund<<ic>> gland polyps

modes.label: Other medical adjective endings
modes.description: The ending of another split adjective such as "constrictive" before a condition name.
modes.example: such processes as constrict<<ive>> pericarditis and spinal cord compression

card.writes: It seems to push toward location words such as peripheral, inner, central and cervical, and away from region words.
card.plain: It fires at the end of a split-up body-part adjective, like the last bit of subcapsular in subcapsular cataracts.
